Subject: Aureum MAP & Dedicated reservation — initial sizing workbook attached

Hi Taylor —

Great speaking last week. Attached is a lightweight MAP and a GPU sizing workbook to make the evaluation->commit discussion concrete. High level proposal:

- Pilot (2 weeks): 2-node pool for integration & perf validation
- Evaluation (4–6 weeks): 8-node pool to run representative workload and quality checks
- Ramp/Commit (start month 3): 16-node committed pool, scale to 24 nodes with burst if needed

Key decision points for Aureum: target peak concurrency, tolerable 95th latency, and preferred term (12 vs 24 months).

Attached: GPU_Sizing_Workbook.xlsx — fill the "expected queries / day" and "avg seq len" tabs and I will return a pricing sketch.

I propose a working session Thursday 1/15 at 10am PT to walk through the workbook and lock MAP milestones. Does that work?

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.inference.com | +1 (415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference — Production-first LLM inference

Connor — thanks, this looks useful. Quick answers:

- We can start the pilot with 2 A100 nodes and run a 10-day integration window.
- For evaluation, our target is sustained 1k qps with p95 under 450ms for text-gen (avg seq len ~128).
- Likely leaning toward a 24-month term if unit economics make sense.

I've attached our internal perf summary (DL_Throughput_Report.pdf) — it includes representative traces and our current latency targets.

Can you sketch a pricing path (pilot pricing, evaluation credit, committed monthly rate at 16 nodes, and burst pricing) so we can run this by procurement?

Also — 1/15 10am PT works for our engineering lead.

Cheers,
Taylor Chen

Taylor — thanks for the perf doc, helpful. See the attached MAP draft (Aureum_MAP_v1.pdf) and a pricing sketch below — this is intended to be a clean starting point for procurement.

Pricing sketch (USD / month) — 16-node committed baseline (A100-equivalent):
- Pilot (2 nodes, 10 days): flat $6,000 (one-off) or apply as credit if commit
- Evaluation (8 nodes, 4 weeks): $35,000 (can be credited back up to $20k against commit)
- Committed 16-node rate: $120,000 / month (24-month term preferred)
- Burst hourly rate above committed: $16 / node-hour (billed per hour; capped monthly at 1.5x committed unit cost)
- Volume discount: 10% off committed baseline after month 6 if usage > 120% of committed average

MAP milestones (from the PDF):
1) Pilot complete (integration & smoke tests) — 1 week after pilot start
2) Eval metrics validated (latency & quality) — 4 weeks after pilot start
3) Exec signoff & PO issued — target by week 8
4) Commit live (16-node pool) — month 3 start

Notes on burst: burst is intended to cover predictable peak events. Burst will be rate-limited by region capacity; in the event of regional shortfall Redwood will offer automatic fallbacks to compatible model variants and provide credits (escalated by ops).

I'm happy to discuss specific term/discount tradeoffs on the call. See you and your engineers at 10am PT.

Best,
Connor

Attachment: Aureum_MAP_v1.pdf (MAP draft; milestones, acceptance criteria, acceptance tests)

Subject: Re: Aureum MAP & Dedicated reservation — final ops notes on burst & monitoring

Hi all — jumping in from Ops to capture what we need on the MAP to make burst behavior safe for both sides: 

- Recommended burst cap: default to 200% of committed average node-hours per calendar month, with an automated alert at 120% and a soft throttle at 250% to avoid runaway costs.
- If burst exceeds 250% and capacity is limited, Redwood will: a) provide compatible model fallbacks, b) issue a pro-rated credit for impacted hours, and c) raise a capacity request with 24h SLA for remediation.
- Monitoring: we will expose per-pool token and node-hour metrics to Aureum's team and provide a shared Grafana link (read-only).

We will include the above in the operational appendix of the MAP. Connor — please confirm the proposed burst cap and I will add the runbook link to the Drive folder.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
